overview.text: The Army's plan to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa is back on after a court lifted a stay, with residents bracing for a lead dust plume.
The Justice Department apologized for a false statement to a judge in the Ilhan Omar home search case.
Kilmar Abrego Garcia is leaving the U.S. for Spain, ending a 20-month legal ordeal after his wrongful deportation last year.
A federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing U.S. trade secrets but acquitted it of racketeering.
Wisconsin reported its third measles death, a day after Pennsylvania's ninth, bringing the U.S. tally to 14.
San Antonio airport says it has enough staff for the Thanksgiving rush, and new nonstop Caribbean flights were announced.

stories.headline: ✅ Spurs 123, Kings 107
stories.summary: Final · at Kings · Record 15-3

stories.headline: San Antonio airport says staffing is enough for Thanksgiving rush
stories.summary: San Antonio International Airport says it has enough staff for holiday travel as hiring continues, and Thanksgiving travel is picking up.
stories.why: Helps if you're flying out this week.

stories.headline: BermudAir launches nonstop San Antonio flights to Belize City, Grand Cayman
stories.summary: Two seasonal nonstop Caribbean routes were announced from San Antonio International Airport.

stories.headline: Mayor says ICE arrest at West Side site had no city link
stories.summary: San Antonio's mayor said an ICE arrest at a West Side waste collection site involved no city association.

stories.headline: Court allows Army's Iowa lead azide detonation to proceed
stories.summary: A court lifted an administrative stay, letting the Army move forward with detonating about five tons of degraded lead azide in Iowa. The plan has gone on, off and on again, with President Trump weighing in.
stories.why: Residents in the plume's path face possible lead dust exposure.

stories.headline: Maps show how far Iowa detonation lead dust could travel
stories.summary: Forecast maps show the plume stretching from near Burlington toward Macon, Missouri, by noon Wednesday. Forecasts will change with the weather.
stories.why: Shows who may need to take precautions.

stories.headline: Alaska ends voter data sharing with Justice Department
stories.summary: Alaska's Republican elections chief ended an agreement that shared the state's detailed voter registration list with the Justice Department, which had used it to flag voters for removal.
stories.why: Raises questions about federal access to voter data.

stories.headline: Justice Dept. apologizes for false statement to judge in Omar case
stories.summary: The department acknowledged the misstatement hours after the House's top lawyer said it mischaracterized his view on constitutional protections for lawmakers.
stories.why: Bears on limits of searches of sitting members of Congress.

stories.headline: Sullivan concedes Alaska Senate race to Peltola
stories.summary: The Republican conceded five days after the Trump administration dropped a long-shot lawsuit meant to potentially block certification of the race.

stories.headline: Trump awards Rudy Giuliani Presidential Medal of Freedom
stories.summary: Trump presented the honor to Giuliani, a longtime ally whose reputation was tarnished by efforts to overturn the 2020 election on Trump's behalf.

stories.headline: Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. for Spain after long legal fight
stories.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongfully deported last year, is self-deporting to Spain. He had faced possible deportation to Liberia.
stories.why: Ends a closely watched immigration case.

stories.headline: Iranian singer receives 74 lashes for performing without hijab
stories.summary: Singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four production team members each received 74 lashes after being convicted of offending public decency, an Iranian news site said.
stories.why: Western governments and rights groups call flogging torture.

stories.headline: Thomas Markle indicted on child sexual abuse material charges
stories.summary: A Los Angeles federal grand jury indicted Thomas Markle, 82, on possession charges. He is expected to be arraigned in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing U.S. trade secrets
stories.summary: A New York federal jury convicted Huawei of stealing trade secrets from companies including T-Mobile and Cisco, but acquitted it of racketeering.

stories.headline: Investigators find Nvidia chips illegally diverted to China
stories.summary: Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, while Attorney General Blanche downplays questions about Nvidia.

stories.headline: FinCEN discloses cybersecurity incident
stories.summary: The Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said unauthorized access hit a limited subset of its systems. It has not shared the scope or source.

stories.headline: Public health guidance on possible lead exposure in Iowa
stories.summary: The Iowa Poison Control Center's medical director explains how people can protect themselves after the Army detonates degraded lead azide.
stories.why: Practical steps for those near the blast.

stories.headline: Medicare hospice caps leave some patients without care
stories.summary: Critics say payment limits penalize patients who are not dying on the government's timetable, leaving some without hospice care.

stories.headline: This group of seamstresses mends shirts to make chemo easier for cancer patients
stories.summary: Seamstresses in Ohio and other states are making zippered shirts for cancer patients so they can more comfortably undergo chemotherapy treatments.

stories.headline: U.S. preparing new tariffs on global trading partners
stories.summary: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.

stories.headline: UK gas prices to rise significantly in January under new cap
stories.summary: Regulator Ofgem's new price cap will push domestic gas prices up significantly in January.

stories.headline: Al Gore buys hometown Tennessee newspaper Carthage Courier
stories.summary: The Lake family, which has run the weekly for five decades, will sell it to the former vice president in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Indiana tumbles from 12-team field in fourth CFP rankings
stories.summary: Upset losses by UCLA and Indiana would leave the Big Ten with one bid if the playoff opened now. Tennessee and Texas jumped Alabama.

stories.headline: Boise State drops out of CFP rankings after late loss
stories.summary: A last-second loss dropped Boise State from 17th to unranked, leaving no Group of 6 team in the rankings.

stories.headline: Broncos suspend J.K. Dobbins one game
stories.summary: Denver suspended Dobbins for conduct detrimental to the team. He will miss Friday's game against the Steelers as Denver holds a slight AFC West lead.

stories.headline: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
stories.summary: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.

stories.headline: Substance released at concert could be linked to robberies, police say
stories.summary: Police are investigating a possible link between the Co-op Live evacuation and reported robberies.

stories.headline: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Review: Golden-Boy Fumes
stories.summary: Quentin Tarantino wrote, and David Fincher directed, this movie starring Brad Pitt, which picks up with the stuntman character he played in “Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood.”

today.summary: Cloudy today, with a high of 56° and a low of 43°. No rain expected.
